ai.title: Allow all OpenRouter models
ai.summary: Backend `modelToAiSDKModel` now defaults unknown models to OpenRouter instead of throwing. `supportsCacheControl` helper replaces hardcoded `openrouter_grok_4` check for prompt caching. Zod schemas for `model` and `agentType` relaxed from strict enums to strings. Error handling in `promptAiSdkStream` now captures `APICallError` response bodies.

eli5.text: When you ask me to use an AI model that I hadn't heard of before, I now quietly route it through OpenRouter instead of refusing and stopping the request. I still use my built-in shortcuts for the big names like OpenAI and Anthropic, but anything else automatically gets sent to OpenRouter by default. While I'm working, I also stopped accidentally dropping the "not allowed" warning when I try to use a tool you didn't unlock, so the message I send back actually matches what I tried to do. If something goes wrong with a request to my AI provider, I now capture the full error details instead of a brief note, which helps figure out why the call failed.

ai.title: Infisical caching in bun wrapper
ai.summary: Added caching for Infisical secrets in .bin/bun using .infisical-cache with 15-minute TTL. Reduces startup from ~1.2s to ~0.16s. Cache invalidates on .infisical.json modification or expiry. Uses infisical export with 10s timeout for session validation. Added .infisical-cache to .gitignore.

eli5.text: When you run a command, the system used to fetch a set of secret passwords from a secure storage tool every single time, which made it take over a second to start. Now, those passwords get temporarily saved in a short-term cache that expires after 15 minutes or whenever the password list changes, so repeated runs start up almost instantly. You wouldn't see anything different except commands that use these secrets will run much faster, and the temporary cache file is automatically kept out of shared project storage to keep the secrets private.

ai.title: Move conversation history message into triggerSpawnAgents
ai.summary: In backend/src/tools/handlers/spawn-agents.ts, the conversationHistoryMessage definition moved inside the triggerSpawnAgents async function. This change ensures the message content is generated only when the spawn operation is triggered, avoiding unnecessary JSON serialization of mutableState.messages if the handler exits early. Internal refactor affecting only the backend agent spawning logic.

eli5.text: The system that starts helper assistants now waits to build the conversation summary until you actually ask it to spawn one, instead of preparing it ahead of time. This means it no longer wastes effort converting the full chat log into a message when the spawn process ends early. If you looked, you'd see the summary-building code moved from the outer setup into the inner trigger that only runs when spawning is confirmed. The change is live today and only affects backend agent startup.

eli5.text: When the assistant kicks off its background helper agents, it now builds the conversation-history context inside the part of the process that actually starts those agents, rather than up front in the main flow. You won't see anything different at runtime: the same history still gets passed along, just assembled closer to where it's used. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes the code easier to follow and safer to run, with no change to what the assistant actually does.

eli5.text: You won't notice anything different: conversations between you and the assistant still come back the same way. Behind the scenes, the system used to quietly cut off part of the conversation history whenever a sub-task was marked finished, then hand the trimmed-down version to the next step. That cut has been removed, so the full set of messages now flows straight into the existing size-limiting step without being pre-trimmed. It's internal housekeeping with no expected change to your experience.

ai.title: Refactor bun wrapper to eliminate cd usage
ai.summary: The `.bin/bun` script now resolves the project root using `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to anchor cache file paths and `infisical export` execution. This replaces direct `cd` commands with subshell execution (`cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && infisical export`) to prevent side effects on the main shell's working directory. The change affects `.bin/bun` and updates `knowledge.md` to document the new subshell isolation mechanism.

eli5.text: When the project-running helper looks for secret settings and cache files, it now figures out the top-level project folder first and does its temporary directory switching inside a separate subshell, so your main terminal window stays in whatever folder you started from. The team also wrote down how this new isolation trick works inside the internal notes. You wouldn't notice anything visually, but the helper is now less likely to leave your terminal in an unexpected folder after it finishes, which keeps later commands from accidentally running in the wrong place.

ai.title: Remove dynamic agent template schema invalid model test
ai.summary: Removed the test case verifying rejection of invalid model names in dynamic agent templates. This cleanup addresses a redundant or failing assertion in the schema validation suite. The change is confined to the common package's test directory.

eli5.text: A specific test that checked whether the system properly rejected misspelled model names has been removed from the code's quality-checking tools. This means the project's automated tests will no longer verify that invalid model names are caught, though the main software itself still rejects them. If you looked at the test run, you'd see one fewer test case being executed, but there's no visible change to how the tool actually works.

ai.title: CI workflow split into parallel setup, build-web, typecheck, and build
ai.summary: The CI pipeline now executes build-web, typecheck, and build as independent parallel jobs gated by a shared setup job, replacing the previous sequential build. This structure reduces total execution time by allowing these tasks to run concurrently on separate runners. The test and test-integration jobs now depend on the completion of all three parallel build jobs rather than a single build step. Dependency caching is centralized in the setup job using bun.lockb hashes to optimize installation across the parallel branches.

eli5.text: When you submit new code, the automated safety check now runs three of its major steps, the web app build, a type check, and the final build, all at the same time on separate computers instead of doing them one after another. After all three finish, the system proceeds to run the regular tests and integration tests, which now wait for every parallel build job to succeed rather than waiting on just one combined build step. You won't see a different result, but the whole process should wrap up faster because the longest-running tasks no longer have to take turns.

ai.title: CI nodemodules artifact replace cache
ai.summary: GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` replaces `actions/cache` and `bun install` steps in build/test jobs with `actions/upload-artifact`/`actions/download-artifact` for `node_modules`. The `setup` job now uploads the installed dependencies as an artifact with 1-day retention, which downstream jobs download instead of re-installing or restoring cache. A stub `.contentlayer/generated/index.ts` is created in the web typecheck job to satisfy build requirements without running the full contentlayer generation.

eli5.text: Starting today, the project's automated build system no longer reinstalls code dependencies from scratch or relies on a shared cache during build and test jobs. Instead, a single setup step installs everything once, uploads that installed package folder as a transferable file, and each later job pulls down that same file to reuse, which is why you would see the download happen faster and more consistently if you watched a build run. Additionally, one check that only verifies code structure now fakes a needed data folder instead of generating real content, since that folder exists only for the final website build. This is internal-only housekeeping, so there is nothing new to use directly.

ai.title: CI artifact actions bumped v3 to v4
ai.summary: actions/upload-artifact and actions/download-artifact bumped v3 to v4 in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Six download steps plus one upload step updated. Internal CI only.

eli5.text: The internal system that runs automated checks on every code change had its helper tools upgraded from one version to the next, which means those checks will now use the newer version of the packaging mechanism. Only the team's own development pipeline is affected; nothing in the product itself changes.

ai.title: Fix CI typecheck stub for contentlayer
ai.summary: Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to generate a valid TypeScript stub for `contentlayer` during CI. The previous stub `export {}` caused typecheck failures because it lacked the expected `allDocs` export. The new stub exports `allDocs` as an empty array typed as `any[]`, satisfying the type checker.

eli5.text: The automated check that makes sure the website code is consistent now passes when checking the content catalog, which had been failing because it was given an empty placeholder instead of the expected list of documents. If you run the full verification today, it completes instead of stopping with an error about the missing document list.

ai.title: Remove contentlayer from CI typecheck
ai.summary: Removed contentlayer generation step from CI workflow and excluded .contentlayer from web/tsconfig.json include paths. This prevents typecheck failures caused by missing or malformed generated contentlayer files. Affects .github/workflows/ci.yml and web/tsconfig.json.

eli5.text: The automated checking process that makes sure the website's code is correct no longer stops to create a temporary helper file before running its checks, and the list of files it keeps an eye on no longer includes that helper's folder. If you looked at the results of this automated check, you would notice it finishes without the extra step of generating those helper files, and any problems that previously made the check fail because those files were missing or broken won't happen anymore. This change is live today as part of the standard automated checks that run behind the scenes.

ai.title: CI: Merge typecheck and web build into parallel job
ai.summary: Consolidated separate CI jobs for typecheck and web build into a single build-and-check job. Both processes now run in parallel using bash background jobs and `wait`, replacing the sequential execution or separate runner overhead. This change reduces CI pipeline duration by eliminating redundant setup steps and optimizing resource usage within the same runner environment.

eli5.text: The team combined two separate automated checking steps that used to run one after the other into a single step where both checks happen at the same time. This affects the internal process that verifies the web app builds correctly and the code types are valid before changes go live. If you looked at the workflow file, you would see one job replacing what used to be two jobs, and both the type checking and web build now run in parallel within the same 10-minute timeout-protected session. This is live today and only affects the internal CI pipeline, not the end-user experience.

ai.title: CI: drop setup job, switch to per-job dependency caching
ai.summary: Removed shared `setup` job and `node_modules` artifact upload/download in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Replaced with `actions/cache@v3` and direct `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in `build-and-check` and test jobs. Key uses `${{ hashFiles('**/bun.lockb') }}` for cache invalidation. Eliminates cross-job artifact transfer overhead.

eli5.text: The development tooling used by the engineering team to automatically test and build the app got simpler and faster behind the scenes. Instead of one shared setup step that downloaded and shipped the app's code libraries to every other step, each independent task now keeps its own small copy locally and only redownloads what changed. Nothing you see as a user changes, but builds and checks finish a bit more efficiently.

ai.title: Add parent instructions to custom agents
ai.summary: Added `parentInstructions` field to `AgentTemplate` and `.agents/templates/*.json`. `DynamicAgentService` validates these instructions against available agents. `collectParentInstructions` aggregates relevant directives from all templates to inject into the parent's `userInputPrompt` under 'Instructions for Spawning Agents'. Includes new `knowledge-keeper` template and refactors base prompts.

eli5.text: A parent agent can now see specific, written instructions for each of its helper agents, so it knows exactly when to spawn each one. These instructions are embedded directly into the agent template files, like adding new rules to a playbook. You would notice this when a parent agent spawns a helper, because it now comes with clear guidance baked into its prompt about the helper's role. The change is live and applies to all templates that include the parent instructions field.

ai.title: Version 1.0.436
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.436. Updates `codebuff` package metadata in `npm-app/release/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The AI coding assistant is now on its latest version, 1.0.436, which bundles together several recent improvements. As of July 19, the assistant can use any model available through OpenRouter instead of only pre-approved ones, and custom AI helpers you build now accept extra guidance that gets passed down to the tasks they delegate. You won't see a new button or menu to tell these changes are live, but when you ask for help or add your own specialized helper, the system handles more models and finer-grained instructions than it did the week before.
